prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: checked baggage from acceptance at bag-drop or transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up and handoff at the outbound load control point; excludes aircraft loading beyond handoff.

Elements:
- Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit: records accepted bags, initiates processing; sends Oversize Exception Ticket when a bag exceeds the configured size envelope.
- Bag Tag Printer: produces a durable tag with a unique identifier per accepted bag.
- Transfer Bag Feeder: identifies inbound transfer bags, records arrival; sends Late Transfer Bag Card when a bag enters from an inbound transfer stream.
- Induction Tray Conveyor: accepts bags through controlled feed points and keeps separation between bags.
- Baggage Control System (alias Velvet): associates tag identifier with passenger/flight record; checks flight open and record complete; compares transfer-bag data with current routing before release.
- Concourse Zone Controller (alias Mosslight): local equipment coordination; produces Recovery Route Card; grants induction permissive only when local equipment status and restrictions allow.
- Flight Data Gateway: sends Flight Cutoff Advisory; supplies flight and routing records.
- Primary Crossbelt Sorter; North Gate Scanner, South Gate Scanner; Image Resolution Desk; Secondary Inspection Chute; Bag Reconciliation Station; East and West Make-Up Conveyors; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit; Outbound Load Control Desk.

Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor (oversees flow, coordinates recovery with Security Duty Manager and Maintenance Technician); Explosives Response Team; Security Duty Manager; Maintenance Technician; Airline Ramp Coordinator; check-in staff.

Items: checked bags, bag tag/identifier, Flight Cutoff Advisory, Recovery Route Card, Oversize Exception Ticket, Late Transfer Bag Card, flight/routing records, induction permissive, equipment status, routing state, operating restrictions.

Requirements: staff confirm eligibility and verify passenger/flight before acceptance; bags with missing/unreadable/conflicting data held for staff resolution before induction; staff check size/weight; oversized bags held until an approved route is confirmed; transfer identifiers must be legible and match a valid onward flight; before induction the bag record must be valid, route available and receiving equipment ready. Objectives: safe screening, accurate bag-to-flight association, predictable throughput, delivery within cutoffs.

Document units:
S045: Interlocks stop feed movement when a jam, access-door opening, or loss of downstream readiness is detected.
S046: The North Gate Scanner reads the bag identifier as the bag enters the screening and sorting network.
S047: The North Gate Scanner is also known locally as Kestrel.
S048: The South Gate Scanner provides an independent read point for bags routed through its assigned entry path.
S049: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter receives inducted bags and directs them according to the active routing data.
S050: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter is also known locally as Juniper.
S051: When automated image review cannot resolve a bag image, staff at the Image Resolution Desk assess the available image and record a disposition.
S052: The Airline Ramp Coordinator sends a Carousel Release Slip when the outbound build is authorized.
S053: The Baggage Control System applies the approved screening profile to each bag using its tag data and the current operating configuration.
S054: The Induction Tray Conveyor presents bags to the screening equipment at a controlled spacing that supports reliable image capture.
S055: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter maintains bag identity and routes each bag according to the screening disposition available at the time of sorting.
S056: The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner acquire screening images and return a disposition for each bag that passes through them.
S057: Screening equipment records image quality and alarm status so that an incomplete examination is not treated as a clear result.
S058: When automated image review cannot resolve a bag image, staff at the Image Resolution Desk assess the available image and record a disposition.
S059: The reviewer considers the full image, bag identification, and any system prompts before assigning a disposition.
S060: A bag remains under controlled routing while its image is awaiting review, and the system prevents it from entering an outbound make-up path prematurely.
S061: The South Gate Scanner produces a Manual Rescan Receipt when a manual rescan is required.
S062: A clear disposition permits normal routing only when the bag identity and screening record agree.
S063: An alarm, an unresolved image, or a missing screening record places the bag into an exception status for additional examination.
S064: The Baggage Control System routes exception-status bags to the Secondary Inspection Chute through a path that avoids normal outbound flows.
S065: The chute is monitored for occupancy so that a bag is not released into a blocked or unavailable inspection position.
